st: Tie or tuck the pork belly into a snug roll. Sear it in a dry pot over medium-high heat until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Add [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce, the mirin, sugar, [[2 cloves]] garlic, half the ginger and [[2 cups]] water. Cover and simmer on low, turning once, until fork tender.
While the pork cooks, boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes, then move them to ice water and peel. Marinate them in a spoonful of the pork braising liquid.
In a large pot, combine the chicken broth, remaining garlic and ginger. Simmer for 20 minutes, then remove the solids.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, then stir it back into the pot along with [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce and the sesame oil. Keep hot.
Slice the cooled pork into thin pieces. Halve the eggs.
Boil the noodles in plenty of unsalted water as the package says, usually 2 to 3 minutes. Drain well.
Divide the noodles among four bowls, ladle the hot broth over, and top with pork, egg halves and scallions. Serve immediately.

ing: tuna or salmon, previously frozen, from a trusted fishmonger
st: Rinse the rice in a bowl, swirling and draining until the water runs almost clear.
Cook the rice with [[2.25 cups]] water in a covered pot: bring to a boil, then simmer on low until the water is absorbed. Rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Warm the vinegar, sugar and salt together until the sugar dissolves, then let it cool.
Tip the hot rice into a wide bowl. Fold in the vinegar mixture with a cutting motion while fanning the rice, until glossy and cooled to body temperature.
Slice the fish into long strips about 0.5 inch thick, using a very sharp knife. Keep it cold until serving.
Place a nori sheet on a bamboo mat. Wet your hands and spread a thin layer of rice over it, leaving a strip at the top clear.
Lay a line of fish and cucumber across the middle. Roll tightly from the bottom, using the mat, and seal with a little water.
Slice each roll into 6 pieces with a wet knife. Serve with wasabi and soy sauce.
Make the dipping sauce: simmer the soy sauce, mirin and [[0.5 cup]] water for 2 minutes. Cool and pour into small bowls.
Cut 3 shallow slits along the belly of each shrimp and press flat so they do not curl. Pat everything dry.
Heat the oil to 340°F (170°C) in a deep pot.
Whisk the egg with the ice water. Add [[1 cup]] flour and salt, and stir only a few strokes. Lumps are fine and keep the batter crisp.
Dust the shrimp and vegetables lightly with flour, then dip them in the batter, letting extra drip off.
Fry in small batches, not crowding the pot, until pale golden and crisp: vegetables 3 to 4 minutes, shrimp 2 minutes.
Drain on a rack, not paper, so they stay crisp. Skim stray batter bits from the oil between batches.
Serve hot right away with the dipping sauce.

ing: made from instant dashi granules or kombu and bonito
st: Soak the dried wakame in a small bowl of cold water for 5 minutes until it expands, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a pot. Do not let it boil hard.
Add the tofu cubes and wakame and warm them for 2 minutes.
Put the miso in a ladle or small bowl and whisk it with some hot broth until fully dissolved.
Turn off the heat and stir the miso into the pot. Never boil miso, since boiling dulls its flavor.
Ladle into bowls, sprinkle with scallions and serve right away.
Cut small slits through the fat edge of each chop to stop it curling, then pound lightly to even thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Mix the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and sugar for the sauce. Set aside.
Set up three plates: flour, beaten eggs, and panko. Coat each chop in flour, then egg, then press firmly into the panko.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 340°F (170°C).
Fry the cutlets two at a time until deep golden and the pork reaches 145°F (63°C), about 5 minutes, turning once.
Drain on a rack and rest for 3 minutes. Cut into strips.
Serve on a pile of shredded cabbage with the sauce on the side, plus steamed rice.
Cook the rice according to its package and keep it warm.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef on all sides, about 6 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Lower to medium and cook the onions in the same pot until soft and golden, about 10 minutes.
Return the beef to the pot, add [[4 cups]] water and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam, then simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the curry roux pieces until melted. Add the apple if using.
Simmer gently on low for 5 more minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy. Add salt if needed.
Serve the curry over the rice.
Whisk the flour, dashi and salt in a large bowl until smooth. Mix in all 4 eggs.
Fold in the cabbage and scallions so everything is coated with batter.
Mix the ketchup and Worcestershire for the sauce. Set aside.
Heat a little oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Scoop in a quarter of the batter and shape into a thick round, about 5 inches wide.
Lay a few pork slices on top. Cook for 5 minutes, until the bottom is golden.
Flip carefully, press gently, and cook 5 more minutes until the pork is crisp and the center is cooked. Repeat for the other 3 pancakes.
Spread with the sauce, drizzle with mayonnaise, and sprinkle with bonito flakes. Serve hot.
Mix the flour and baking powder, then whisk in the dashi, eggs and soy sauce until a thin, smooth batter forms. Rest it in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Mix the ketchup and Worcestershire for the sauce.
Heat a takoyaki pan over medium-high heat and brush all the holes with oil.
Fill each hole to the top with batter. Drop a piece of octopus into each, then sprinkle with scallions and ginger.
Cook 2 minutes until the edges set, then use a skewer to push the batter around the edge into the holes and turn each ball.
Keep turning the balls until they are round, golden and crisp outside, about 6 more minutes.
Pile onto a plate, brush with the sauce, drizzle with mayonnaise and top with bonito flakes. Let them cool a minute, since the centers stay very hot.
Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil for the noodles.
In another pot, combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, salt and sugar. Bring to a simmer and keep warm for 10 minutes.
Cook the udon in the boiling water, following the package timing, usually 2 to 4 minutes for frozen.
Drain the noodles and rinse briefly under hot water to remove surface starch.
Divide the noodles among four deep bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles.
Top each with a piece of tempura and the sliced scallions. Serve immediately so the tempura stays crisp.

ing: for filling, plus more for dipping
st: Toss the chopped cabbage with the salt and let it sit for 10 minutes. Squeeze out as much water as you can with your hands.
Mix the cabbage with the pork, garlic, ginger, scallions, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce and sesame oil until sticky.
Place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the middle of a wrapper. Wet the edge with a fingertip of water.
Fold in half and pleat the edge in a few folds, pressing firmly to seal. Repeat with all wrappers.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Arrange the gyoza flat-side down and cook until the bottoms are golden, about 3 minutes.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] water, cover immediately and steam on medium until the water has cooked off.
Uncover and cook 1 more minute to re-crisp the bottoms. Check the pork is cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Mix some soy sauce with the rice vinegar for dipping and serve.
Pat the chicken dry. Poke the skin a few times with a fork so the sauce can reach the meat.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar and ginger in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 6 minutes.
Flip and cook 5 more minutes on the other side.
Wipe out excess fat with paper towel. Pour in the sauce, lower the heat to medium and bring to a simmer.
Cook, spooning the sauce over the chicken, until it thickens into a glaze and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C), about 5 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, then slice. Serve over rice with the glaze and scallions.
Rinse the rice, swirling and draining until the water runs nearly clear.
Cook the rice with [[2.25 cups]] water in a covered pot: bring to a boil, then simmer on low until absorbed. Rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise and a pinch of salt. Keep the salmon and umeboshi in separate small bowls.
Let the rice cool just enough to handle. Wet your hands and rub a little salt on your palms.
Scoop about half a cup of rice into your palm and press a hollow in the middle. Add a spoonful of one filling.
Cover with a bit more rice. Cup your hands and press and turn it into a triangle, firmly but gently.
Wrap each onigiri with a strip of nori at the base. Repeat to make 8, and serve the same day.
